headline: ExxonMobil invests additional $6.8 billion in Stabroek project in Guyana | AKM EN
summary_text: The American oil and gas company Exxon Mobil Corp. (ExxonMobil) has made the final investment decision for the development of the Hammerhead field offshore Guyana after receiving regulatory approvals. This is reported in a press release from ExxonMobil. Exxon Mobil is investing an additional $6.8 billion in the Stabroek project, which will include 18 production and injection wells using an FPSO floating vessel with a capacity of 150,000 barrels of oil per day. The seventh project at the Stabroek offshore block of the Hammerhead field is scheduled to be commissioned in 2029. By 2030, the total capacity of ExxonMobil's eight projects in Guyana is estimated at 1.7 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. The latest investment decision increases the amount of funds allocated for the implementation of seven approved projects to $60 billion. Since the start of production at the Stabroek block in 2019, more than $7.8 billion has been invested in Guyana's Natural Resource Fund. As part of the project, ExxonMobil launched its fourth oil production facility, FPSO THE ONE GUYANA, which joined FPSO Destiny, Unity and Prosperity, increasing the total installed capacity to 900,000 barrels of oil per day. The fifth and sixth approved Uaru and Whiptail projects are currently underway, with Uaru starting production in 2026 and Whiptail in 2027. ExxonMobil's subsidiary Guyana Limited is the operator of the project and owns 45% of the shares in the Stabroek block. At the same time, Hess Guyana Exploration Ltd. controls 30% of the shares, and CNOOC Petroleum Guyana Limited controls 25%. From the point of view of ExxonMobil management, the Stabroek project plays an important role for the Government of Guyana, given the employment of 70% of the workforce and 2,000 local enterprises in the oil and gas industry in Guyana. Since 2015, ExxonMobil Guyana has paid more than $2.9 billion to Guyanese suppliers. ExxonMobil is one of the largest multinational oil and gas companies in the world by market capitalization ($400 billion). The company is engaged in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and natural gas, including the sale of lubricants under the Mobil brand and fuels under the Exxon, Mobil and Esso brands. The main oil reserves are located in Asia and the USA, while natural gas reserves are located in the USA, Australia, Asia and Europe. The headquarters is located in Irving, Texas.

headline: Exxon turns to automated drilling in the Permian in push for higher oil output | MarketScreener Canada
summary_text: MIDLAND, Texas, Aug 24 (Reuters) - In rural west Texas where oil rigs and pump jacks dot the sparse flat landscape, an ExxonMobil contractor sits in a small office on a drilling rig, using controls on a screen to ... robotic machinery and move tall steel ... weighing roughly 2,000 pounds. This work would usually require human overseers standing on the rig floor, the most common location for accidents on a rig. Exxon, the largest oil producer by volume in the U.S., operates more than 30 drilling rigs in the Permian Basin, two of which are automated rigs with robotic equipment. By 2028, the company aims to transition half of its fleet to automated rigs to reduce the need for workers to perform potentially dangerous work and increase efficiency to drill wells faster, an executive told Reuters. The Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico, the biggest U.S. oilfield, revolutionized energy markets two decades ago when development of the shale basin turned the U.S. into one of the leading oil-producing countries. But the relatively quick decline rate of shale wells has prompted drillers to develop more technologies to extract the oil. Some in the industry are also concerned about when the Permian's production could begin to decline. Exxon plans to grow its Permian production by almost 40% to 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030. By contrast, rival oil major Chevron plans to hold production steady at about 1 million boepd, focusing instead on free cash flow. The automated drilling rigs are part of a combination of technologies and strategies Exxon is using to boost production, said Bart Cahir, Exxon's senior vice president of unconventionals, in an interview on the rig. "When we take people off the rig floor, those same individuals are now able to think ahead and plan for the next operation and that combination gives us efficiency," he said. "This is the productivity play." The company installed its first automated rig, supplied by drilling contractor Helmerich & Payne, last year. It drilled two miles horizontally underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history. Exxon's use of automated rigs in the Permian and its goal of expanding the fleet has not been previously reported. ... . Employees on ... . Removing workers from the so-called Red Zones allows them to focus on other operations on the rig and reduces variability in the work, meaning more feet per day can be drilled, Cahir said. "In the history of well drilling activity, about a third of significant injuries that occur happen on the rig floor," he said. "By getting people out of that higher risk area, we're essentially eliminating that risk." Exxon plans to expand automated rigs to a quarter of the fleet next year and then half of the fleet by 2028, Cahir said. ... Exxon is also developing a suite of more than 40 technologies to double its oil recovery from the Permian by the early 2030s. The shale industry typically extracts just 10% of the oil in the ground due to the tight, compacted rock. (Reporting by Sheila Dang in Midland, Texas; Editing by David Gregorio)

headline: ExxonMobil Proposes $80 Billion Kashagan West Venture Wit...
summary_text: # ExxonMobil Proposes $80 Billion Kashagan West Venture With KazMunayGas Targeting 600,000 Bpd From Kazakhstan Caspian Reserves ... ExxonMobil proposed an $80 billion Kashagan West venture with KazMunayGas targeting 600,000 bpd, pending resolution of Kazakhstan's $150 billion arbitration. ... ExxonMobil has formally proposed an $80 billion joint venture with KazMunayGas to develop the untapped western portion of Kazakhstan's Kashagan oil field in the Caspian Sea. The venture targets production of 600,000 barrels per day from reserves ExxonMobil estimates at roughly 10 billion barrels. One condition controls the entire deal: Kazakhstan must first resolve a $150 billion international arbitration claim and a separate $5 billion environmental fine against current Kashagan operators. ... ExxonMobil holds a 16.81% stake in the existing Kashagan eastern section, which currently produces approximately 450,000 barrels per day, according to World Oil. The western section remains entirely undeveloped. ExxonMobil has proposed offering minority stakes to existing Kashagan consortium partners as part of the new venture structure. ... Kazakhstan's government claims roughly $150 billion in revenue lost to development delays at Kashagan over two decades. That claim is in international arbitration. A separate $5 billion environmental fine has been levied against the consortium, of which ExxonMobil, Eni, Shell, TotalEnergies, and CNPC are all members. The government has made clear that new investment approvals depend on resolving both matters. ... The scale of the dispute dwarfs the proposed investment. ExxonMobil's $80 billion offer equals roughly 53 cents for every dollar Kazakhstan claims it is owed. Whether Astana treats this venture as compensation or as consideration separate from the arbitration will likely determine whether a final investment decision is reachable by 2030. ... The current Kashagan consortium divides the field across seven parties. ExxonMobil, Eni, Shell, and TotalEnergies each hold 16.81%. KazMunayGas, the state operator, holds 16.88%. China National Petroleum Corporation carries 8.4%, and Inpex holds the remaining 7.56%. The proposed Kashagan West venture would maintain KazMunayGas as the host-state partner while offering existing shareholders minority positions in the new development. ... ExxonMobil's 16.81% stake in an eastern section producing 450,000 bpd translates to roughly 75,600 barrels per day of equity production. If the western section reaches its 600,000 bpd target and ExxonMobil holds a comparable interest, the company would add another 100,000-plus barrels per day of Caspian equity output. That would rank Kashagan West among ExxonMobil's largest single project additions outside the Permian Basin. ... At $80 billion for 600,000 barrels per day of target production, the venture implies a capital cost of roughly $133,333 per daily barrel of capacity. That figure is two to three times the capital intensity of a typical Permian Basin horizontal well program. Kashagan's complexity justifies the premium: the field's crude carries 19% hydrogen sulphide content by weight, among the highest of any commercially producing reservoir in the world. ... Kazakhstan already carries significant overproduction pressure within the OPEC+ framework. Compensatory cut obligations ran from 503,000 barrels per day in January 2026 to 669,000 barrels per day in June, as Oil Authority reported in its OPEC+ compliance analysis. Much of Kazakhstan's production reduction reflected infrastructure disruptions rather than voluntary restraint, per that reporting. Adding 600,000 new barrels per day at peak Kashagan West output would deepen the country's OPEC+ compliance burden when the project eventually comes online. ... ExxonMobil reported $14.7 billion in adjusted Q2 2026 earnings, with the Pioneer Natural Resources integration driving free cash flow to $17.2 billion for the quarter, as Oil Authority covered in its Q2 earnings analysis. That cash generation gives the company leverage to fund the $250 million concept study and an estimated $2 billion in front-end engineering design work scheduled to begin in 2028. A final investment decision is targeted for 2030 at the earliest.

headline: ExxonMobil confirms US$55B investment in Guyana recovered - Kaieteur News

President of ExxonMobil Guyana Limited, Alistair Routledge ... What we are now seeing in this price environment is that will accelerate.” ... Be that as it may, the Country Manager did not specifically highlight Guyana’s share moving to 50%. Instead, Routledge said, “ If you stay at the current oil price then it will happen this year based on the level of expenditures and the production that we anticipate so that’s a significant acceleration. What that then means is that instead roughly the 14 and a half percent that the country has been receiving by way of revenues into the Natural Resource Fund from the Stabroek production and revenues, what will happen is that percentage will significantly increase.” ... At that time, he told reporters approximately US$5B was still to be recovered. ... Subsequently, in June, Kaieteur News reported based on an in-house analysis that Guyana has paid off ExxonMobil the full cost of seven oil projects approved to date by government. ... Using an average oil price of US$80 per barrel, considering daily production for the year so far at approximately 900,000 barrels per day (bpd), the Stabroek Block generated approximately US$12.3B in revenue up to 20 th June, 2026. ... According to the oil deal, 75% of revenue is dedicated to cost, as such, it could be estimated that US$9.2B went towards cost, far more than the US$5B that needed to be recovered according to Exxon. ... This means that Guyana should already be receiving its full 50% profits outlined in the PSA as the cost of all seven oil projects sanctioned by the GoG has been repaid. ... Notably, the major development in Guyana’s petroleum sector was announced by Exxon to its shareholders while government has not said a word to the nation regarding the increased revenue flow into the Natural Resource Fund (NRF) as a result of the cost bank now being empty. ... The government has repeatedly praised itself for its “transparent” management of the industry, yet this major development, expected to significantly impact the country’s revenue generation was not shared with the public. ... Then the court reversed itself two months later, tossing out the ruling and removing a $10 million potential penalty. Operations paused again in July, then resumed in August after a settlement with state authorities. ... If you were watching the stock price, the legal drama looked like a headline event. If you look at the company's actual earnings, something else emerges: Sigma LithiumSGML-- is now posting record margins at the exact same time it's repeatedly forced to negotiate its right to keep mining. ... Sigma's second quarter of 2026 tells a different story than the court filings. Revenue hit a record $55 million on 24,400 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate sold. EBITDA margin reached 47 percent — the highest in the company's history, up from 39 percent in Q1. Gross margin held at 60 percent, operating margin at 32 percent. Total costs fell more than 30 percent quarter over quarter, driven by scale and discipline. All-in sustaining costs dropped to $668 per tonne of lithium carbonate equivalent, down 6 percent from Q1. ... These are not the financials of a company being squeezed by regulatory disruption. They're the financials of a producer ramping volume, catching rising commodity prices, and running a lean operation. The realized price per tonne jumped 17 percent quarter over quarter to $2,089, and the broader lithium market has rallied roughly 100 percent year over year after a brutal 2024-2025 price collapse. ... Production was 35,400 tonnes in Q2, up 50 percent from the prior period. The company has pushed its 12-month production guidance of 240,000 tonnes forward by three months. A Phase 2 expansion is under way to nearly double capacity to 520,000 tonnes annually, with Phase 3 targeting 830,000 tonnes by end of 2028. ... The balance sheet is tightening: net debt fell to $125 million from $134 million in Q1, down 25 percent year over year and 43 percent over two years. Cash sits at $17 million. ... In December 2025, Brazil's Ministry of Labor initiated an administrative inquiry into waste piles at Sigma's Grota do Cirilo mine. Three piles were suspended. Media reports surfaced alleging a "partial rupture" near a school in Poco Dantas. Sigma denied wrongdoing and called the coverage part of a coordinated misinformation campaign. ... In May 2026, labor inspectors fined Sigma for depositing waste on a previously shut-down pile they said posed "grave and imminent risk". A local judge issued a decision with a $10 million potential collateral. Shares fell 15 percent in a single day. ... On June 9, the Court of Justice of Minas Gerais overturned the lower-court ruling. The $10 million requirement was removed. The court ordered Sigma to fund an independent technical advisory firm. Shares rose 4.6 percent. ... Then in mid-July 2026, operations paused again. Not because of the old court case, but because of a new set of environmental fines totaling roughly $540,000 — related to issues from 2013 to 2022, years before Sigma owned the site. The company agreed to pay the fines and cover about $1 million in environmental procedure adjustments, then negotiated a TAC Agreement (a conduct-adjustment term, essentially a settlement) with the state of Minas Gerais. On August 21, the TAC was signed and operations resumed fully. ... This is not a one-time event that got resolved. It's a cycle: operate, get challenged, negotiate, resume. Each cycle interrupts production ramp-up timing, even if the underlying legal position eventually resolves in Sigma's favor. The company now has an independent monitoring firm watching its operations — a permanent cost and a permanent layer of scrutiny. ... Sigma Lithium has one producing mine. It is in Brazil. That concentration works both ways. ... On the positive side, the Grota do Cirilo operation is one of the largest hard-rock lithium sites in the Americas, and the expansion plan leverages existing infrastructure for relatively low incremental capital expenditure. The company describes its Greentech processing plant as using 100 percent water reuse, zero tailings dams, zero toxic chemicals, and 100 percent renewable power. If that model holds up under independent monitoring, it could be a structural cost advantage over wet-chemistry competitors. ... On the risk side, there is no hedge against Brazil-specific disruption. Compare Sigma to Albemarle, which produces across Nevada, Chile, and Australia, or to Arcadia Minerals with Canadian and Australian assets. When a single country's regulators can pause your only revenue source three times in twelve months, diversification isn't a nice-to-have — it's the difference between a manageable delay and an existential pause. Sigma has $1.38 billion in market capitalization, $125 million in net debt, and $17 million in cash. That liquidity cushion is thin if the July-August cycle repeats and the resumption takes months instead of weeks. ... Valuation is hard on a company that reports losses on a trailing basis despite strong quarterly cash generation. Sigma's revenue over the last twelve months is approximately $110 million, and the company reported net losses around $50 million — a drag from depreciation, interest, and non-cash charges on a growing capital base. That makes traditional P/E comparisons misleading. ... Albemarle, the sector anchor, trades at a $14.9 billion market cap with an EV/EBITDA of roughly 17x and a dividend yield near 1.3 percent. It's a proven, diversified, cash-flowing business trading at a premium. Sigma's market cap of roughly $1.38 billion is roughly 9 percent of Albemarle's, despite a Phase 2 expansion that could nearly double its output. The discount reflects both the loss-making earnings picture and the concentrated regulatory risk. ... to anchor it ... The headline about the court ruling has run its course. The ruling was overturned, the fines were settled, the mine is open, and production is ramping. The useful story for investors is no longer whether Sigma wins or loses a legal case. It's whether the company's margin trajectory can survive the regulatory cycle it's embedded in. ... Right now, the factor stack is mixed but tilting positive. Revenue and margin growth are strong. Cost structure is improving. Lithium prices are rising. The 50-day moving average is below the current price, and the RSI sits around 55 — neutral momentum. Net debt is falling. Production guidance is being pushed forward. ... The weak spots are concentration, thin cash, and a regulatory environment that has demonstrated it can interrupt operations even when the company is legally in the right. A $17 million cash position against $125 million of net debt means the company has limited runway if the TAC cycle repeats and production stalls. ... For a watch list, Sigma Lithium belongs in the high-beta lithium sleeve — a name that gives you direct exposure to lithium price recovery at a lower cost basis than the diversified majors. It's not a holding for someone who needs regulatory predictability. The stock rewards conviction in the lithium market and tolerance for emerging-market governance risk. If lithium prices hold above their current levels and the next TAC negotiation concludes within weeks rather than months, the margin expansion could re-rate this stock meaningfully. If the regulatory cycle lengthens or lithium softens, the thin balance sheet makes it vulnerable.

headline: Sigma Lithium (TSXV: SGML) targets 240,000t after Minas Gerais settlement
summary_text: # Sigma Lithium (TSXV: SGML) targets 240,000t after Minas Gerais settlement The Minas Gerais agreement returns Sigma Lithium’s mining and industrial operations to full activity while preserving FY27’s 330,000-tonne production target. ... Sigma Lithium Corporation (TSXV: SGML) has fully resumed mining and industrial operations at its Grota do Cirilo complex in Brazil after signing a Terms for Adjustment of Procedures agreement with the State of Minas Gerais, removing a regulatory overhang that had partially interrupted activity while leaving product sales from reprocessed tailings and intermediate materials unaffected. The company is maintaining a target of producing 240,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate over the next 12 months and 330,000 tonnes in FY27. ... The agreement comes with direct financial obligations but at a scale that appears manageable relative to the operating programme. Sigma Lithium estimates approximately US$1 million of capital expenditure will be required to implement agreed environmental adjustments and has accepted up to US$540,000 of fines relating to environmental matters dating from 2013 to 2022. The company continues to deny wrongdoing regarding key claims while agreeing to specified remedial measures, including widening and gravelling access roads. ... The distinction between settlement and admission is important. Sigma Lithium explicitly disputes several allegations associated with the regulatory issues and said it has not misrepresented environmental filings since 2018 or commercially sold lithium materials before May 2023. The company nevertheless agreed to the TAC requirements in order to resolve the matters and obtain greater operating certainty. ... Sales of high-purity lithium fines produced from reprocessed tailings and other intermediate-grade products continued during the partial suspension, meaning the regulatory issue did not represent a complete commercial shutdown. Full resumption now restores the mining and primary industrial activities required to support the company’s larger production targets. ... Management has retained the 240,000-tonne target for the next 12 months and 330,000 tonnes for FY27, but those remain forward-looking production objectives rather than guaranteed output. Sigma Lithium is upgrading its haulage fleet with equipment manufacturer SANY, including 75-tonne trucks and 98-tonne excavators, to support higher mine throughput. ... The existing Grota do Cirilo operation has annualised nameplate capacity of 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate. Sigma Lithium has also initiated a Phase 2 expansion designed to lift capacity to 580,000 tonnes, followed by a planned Phase 3 that could increase capacity further to 830,000 tonnes. ... Sigma Lithium shares closed at C$16.03 on the TSX Venture Exchange on August 21, up 8.09% from C$14.83. The stock reached C$16.50 intraday, with trading volume of roughly 74,000 shares. ... The positive reaction is consistent with investors removing some regulatory-risk discount after full operations resumed. The TAC provides defined obligations and costs rather than leaving the company in an open-ended negotiation with Minas Gerais authorities, while the retained production guidance indicates management does not currently expect the interruption to derail its FY27 target. ... The shares are nevertheless only modestly above their August 17 close of C$15.82 and remain exposed to lithium-price volatility as well as company-specific execution. The restart resolves one immediate issue; it does not remove commodity risk, expansion funding requirements or the operational challenge of moving toward substantially higher production. ... Production delivery now becomes the clearest measure. Sigma Lithium needs to demonstrate that resumed mine activity, fleet upgrades and plant operations can support the targeted 240,000 tonnes during the next 12 months without another material regulatory or operational interruption. ... The second issue is expansion discipline. Moving from current 330,000-tonne nameplate capacity toward 580,000 tonnes and eventually 830,000 tonnes would materially alter the company’s scale, but expansion creates additional capital, construction and market risks, particularly in a lithium industry where prices can move sharply during project-development cycles. ... The TAC agreement is therefore important because it changes the immediate question facing Sigma Lithium. Investors no longer have to focus primarily on when full operations will restart; attention can return to whether the company can translate its installed capacity and planned expansion into sustained tonnes, margins and cash flow.

Register for the call at https://ir.sigmalithiumcorp.com/events Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - August 14, 2026) - Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or the "Company"), the largest producer of lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹ and dedicated to industrializing lithium materials to supply global producers of batteries for energy security in a responsible manner, announces the Company's results for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and provides an update on recent developments. RECORD REVENUES AND EBITDA MARGINS In 2Q 26, Sigma Lithium achieved gross margin of 60%, maintaining high levels of 1Q26 (at 61%). EBITDA margin at 47% was the highest in the Company’s history, further improving on the 39% margin of 1Q 26. Revenues of US$55 million were also at a record high, up from US$42 million in 1Q 26. Sigma Lithium sold 24,400t in 2Q 26 and commercial flexibility improved the realized price by 17% to US$2,089 (SC5) from US$1,790 in 1Q 26. These costs have the potential to be further decreased as the operational ramp-up continues DECREASED TOTAL DEBT BY 25% WITHIN LAST YEAR In 2Q 26, Sigma Lithium continued to reduce its debt levels, with net debt cut to US$125 million from US$134 million at the end of 1Q 26. The Company remained focused on progressively repaying its higher-cost, short-term export financing facilities. Total debt at the end of 2Q 26 declined by 43% in two years. Sigma Lithium’s cash position stood at US$17 million as of June 30, 2026. Sigma Lithium is currently evaluating a range of financing alternatives, several of which have emerged as a result of the successful mining ramp up and maintained positive sentiment about lithium markets this year. TAC AGREEMENT UNDERWAY Since the week started July 17, 2026, mining and plant operations have been temporarily paused as part of a partial suspension, pending the closing with the Minas Gerais state government of a terms for adjustment of procedures ("Termo de Ajuste de Conduta" or "TAC Agreement"). A TAC Agreement is a standardized form of agreement, that must be mutually agreed between federal and state regulatory bodies and the company. The TAC Agreement is designed to address certain issues raised by the Vale do Jequitinhonha branch of the Minas Gerais state environmental enforcement body. Once the TAC Agreement is finalized, the Company expects to resume mining activities. Sigma Lithium's expectation is that this will occur in the near term. Operations related to the sale of high-purity lithium fines, consisting of reprocessed tailings generated by previous production, have continued without disruption. As noted above, the ramp-up of mining operations following its primarization commenced in January 2026, involved the phased deployment of increasingly larger mining equipment. Once mining activities resume following the current suspension, the Company expects to continue to increase mining haulage capacity and implement the next phase of equipment upgrades. TAC AGREEMENT BACKGROUND On July 22, 2026 Sigma Lithium announced that the Company started negotiating the TAC Agreement with the Minas Gerais state government. The negotiations follow a notification by the Vale do Jequitinhonha regional branch of the Minas Gerais state environmental agency, based in the town of Diamantina, which included the issuing of fines totaling approximately US$540,000 and required a partial suspension of the Company's operations. Several fines were related to environmental issues that occurred from 2013 to 2022. Sigma Lithium vehemently denies any wrongdoing with respect to the key claims raised in connection with the Company's operations . Sigma Lithium reaffirms that the Company: a) has not misrepresented any information filed with the environmental authorities since 2018; b) has not commercially sold any lithium materials prior to May 2023; and c) denies the claims alleging that 2 houses located outside of Sigma Lithium's licensed area are negatively impacted by its activities. The Company agreed to the payment of up to US$540,000 for the above mentioned fines. In parallel to negotiating the TAC Agreement, Sigma Lithium has filed a significant amount of factual and quantitative environmental evidence supporting its defense to the claims related to its current operations with FEAM, the environmental regulator of Minas Gerais state. The Company estimates that the execution of the proposed adjustments of environmental procedures under the TAC Agreement will require an estimated capex of approximately US$1,000,000, mainly related to germination and grassing of the waste rock piles near the south mining pit. INCREASED PLANT 1 CAPACITY LOWERED REALIZED COSTS Following the successfully conclusion of a ramp up of mining operations following the primarization of 4Q 25, and considering the temporary suspension mentioned above, Sigma Lithium has moved forward by a quarter its twelve-month production guidance of 240,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate. The Company is providing production guidance of 330,000 tonnes for the full year of 2027, assuming only Plant 1 is operating throughout the year. This is higher than the original Plant 1 annual nominal capacity of 270,000 tonnes, reflecting productivity improvements in the reprocessing circuit from a steady flow of spodumene being delivered to the industrial plant. This frequent cadence was a result of the successful ramp up of mining operations Sigma Lithium lowered guidance for total cash costs costs per tonne to reflect the lower AISC costs achieved in 2Q 26. Sigma Lithium remains committed to delivering strong near-term growth. Primarily to reflect the recent temporary suspension of operations, the Company has pushed forward the completion of the construction of its next industrial plant to the end of 2027. The Company also expects that it will be able to initiate construction of a third industrial plant next year, completing it by the end of 2028. Plants 2 and 3 will add another 250,000 tonnes of annual capacity each, taking total capacity to 830,000 tonnes per year. headline: Ecovyst Completes Acquisition of Calabrian, Expanding Position as a Leading Provider of Sulfur-Based Chemistries and Technologies
summary_text: WAYNE, Pa., June 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ecovyst Inc. (NYSE: ECVT), a leading provider of virgin sulfuric acid and regenerated sulfuric acid products and services ("Ecovyst"), announced today that it has completed its acquisition of the Calabrian sulfur dioxide and related sulfur derivatives business ("Calabrian") from INEOS Enterprises. ... The Calabrian acquisition expands Ecovyst's capabilities into sulfur dioxide and related derivatives, further diversifying the company's portfolio and end use exposures. Calabrian strengthens Ecovyst's presence in core applications such as mining and water treatment while providing entry into attractive adjacent industry applications, including food processing and pharmaceuticals. ... "The completion of the Calabrian acquisition marks an important step in expanding Ecovyst's capabilities beyond sulfuric acid into sulfur dioxide and related derivatives," said Kurt J. Bitting, Ecovyst's Chief Executive Officer. "This transaction expands our platform of leading sulfur solutions by diversifying our product portfolio, enhancing our participation in attractive end use applications, and supporting our strategies focused on driving higher-value growth for the benefit of our stockholders. We expect Calabrian's strong margins and cash generation capability, together with identified synergy opportunities, to contribute meaningfully to our future financial performance. We are pleased to welcome the Calabrian team to Ecovyst, and we look forward to leveraging their expertise as we execute on our growth strategies on a combined basis." ... Our family of virgin sulfuric acid products, sulfuric acid regeneration services and related derivatives serve a wide range of industrial applications. We are a leading provider of sulfuric acid recycling to the North American refining industry for the production of alkylate, an essential gasoline component for lowering vapor pressure and increasing octane to meet stringent gasoline specifications and fuel efficiency standards. We are a leading North American producer of high quality and high strength virgin sulfuric acid for industrial and mining applications. Through our Calabrian business, we are also a leading producer of sulfur dioxide and related derivatives in North America, serving key end uses including mining, water treatment and specialty chemical production. We also provide chemical waste handling and treatment services, as well as ex-situ catalyst activation services for the refining and petrochemical industry. ... HPCL officials said the expansion would encourage consumers to shift from LPG cylinders to PNG by providing an uninterrupted fuel supply, improved safety and greater convenience. ... According to the company, PNG supply has already commenced in several parts of the Kalyani subdivision, including Gayeshpur, Kataganj and Shaguna Gram Panchayat, where households are gradually adopting piped natural gas as an alternative to conventional LPG cylinders. ... HPCL said the latest initiatives would further strengthen the City Gas Distribution network across Nadia and North 24 Parganas while supporting the Centre’s vision of building a gas-based economy. ... The projects are aligned with the Government of India’s target of increasing the share of natural gas in the country’s energy basket to 15 per cent by 2030. ... Company officials said the expansion of PNG infrastructure would promote cleaner, safer and more sustainable energy solutions for urban households across West Bengal.

headline: Instamart Partners with HPCL to Launch India's First On-Demand LPG Cylinder Delivery Service - CXO Digitalpulse
summary_text: Quick commerce platform Instamart has partnered with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) to introduce what the companies describe as India’s first on-demand LPG cylinder delivery service through a quick commerce platform. The service has been rolled out as a pilot in Bengaluru, allowing consumers to order cooking gas cylinders directly through the Instamart app, extending quick commerce beyond groceries and household essentials into a regulated utility category. ... The initial rollout offers customers a choice between HPCL’s newly launched 10 kg HP Navya composite LPG cylinder and the 5 kg metal LPG cylinder. Unlike conventional domestic LPG services, the offering does not require users to have an existing HP Gas connection, making it accessible to a broader set of consumers, including students, working professionals, small households and those seeking an additional cooking gas cylinder. The companies have not disclosed pricing details for the service. ... The launch also marks the commercial debut of HP Navya, HPCL’s next-generation composite LPG cylinder. Designed to be lighter than conventional cylinders, HP Navya features a corrosion-resistant body and a translucent outer shell that enables customers to monitor the remaining gas level. According to HPCL, the cylinder has been developed with enhanced safety features while offering greater portability for urban households. ... Customers can place orders through the Instamart application by selecting either the 10 kg composite cylinder or the 5 kg metal cylinder. The first purchase is treated as a new cylinder purchase, while subsequent orders are processed as refills, with customers required to return the empty HPCL cylinder at the time of delivery. Orders will be fulfilled through HPCL’s authorised distributor network and delivered by trained personnel in accordance with applicable safety and regulatory protocols. First-time buyers will also be required to complete identity verification before delivery. ... Amit Garg, Director – Marketing, HPCL, said, “Customer needs are evolving, and HPCL is committed to provide innovative solutions to meet them. We are making LPG more accessible and convenient for Naya Bharat with focus on safety, trust and reliability that customers associate HP Gas with.” He added, “HP Navya, our new Composite LPG Cylinder brand, reflects our commitment to delivering innovative energy solutions that make everyday life simpler and more convenient. Through the Instamart platform, we will be able to reach customers through a fast, convenient and digitally enabled platform, making HP Navya Composite LPG Cylinders more accessible while enhancing the overall customer experience.” ... The collaboration reflects the continued expansion of India’s quick commerce sector into new product categories that require specialised fulfilment and regulatory compliance. For Instamart, which already offers a catalogue of more than 50,000 products, LPG delivery represents a move into essential utility services. For HPCL, the partnership introduces an additional digital distribution channel aimed at improving accessibility and convenience for consumers. The companies said the Bengaluru pilot will serve as the initial phase before the service is considered for expansion to additional cities.

headline: India’s Refining Boom: New Petrochemical Capacity Cycle Begins with HPCL Rajasthan Refinery
summary_text: The dedication of the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited’s (HRRL) integrated refinery-cum-petrochemical complex at Pachpadra in Rajasthan’s Balotra district by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 7 has kick-started a new wave of refining capacity expansion in India and marks a defining moment in the country’s energy security ambitions. It is also the first greenfield refinery to be commissioned in India in over a decade. ... Conceived as India’s first greenfield integrated refinery-cum-petrochemical complex, the 9 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA) facility has been developed as a joint venture between Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and the Government of Rajasthan. Driven by the country’s steadily rising demand for petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel, public sector oil marketing companies are embarking on another round of capacity expansion. Including the newly commissioned HRRL refinery, nearly 32 MMTPA of additional refining capacity is expected to come on stream in the near term. ... The biggest expansion is being undertaken by Indian Oil Corporation, which is adding 17.3 MMTPA across its Panipat, Gujarat, Barauni and Paradip refineries. Numaligarh Refinery is expanding its capacity in phases from 3 MMTPA to 9 MMTPA in Assam. Bharat Petroleum plans to expand its Bina refinery to around 11-12 MMTPA, while HPCL-Mittal Energy Limited (HMEL), the joint venture between HPCL and Mittal Energy, is also increasing capacity by 0.5 MMTPA.

headline: India’s first by-design grassroots integrated refining complex reaches startup | Oil & Gas Journal
summary_text: HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Ltd. (HRRL), a 74-26% joint venture of Hindustan Petroleum Corp. Ltd. (HPCL) and the state government of Rajasthan, has officially commissioned its long-planned 9-million tonne/year (tpy) integrated refinery and petrochemical complex at Pachpadra Tehsil in Balotra, Barmer District, Rajasthan. ... Designed with flexibility to process a mix of local and imported crudes, the new complex is equipped to produce Bharat Stage 6-grade fuels (equivalent to Euro 6-quality) from a feedstock of both locally produced and Saudi Arabian crudes to meet increased demand for petroleum products in Rajasthan as well as other northern Indian states.

headline: Modi inaugurates Rajasthan refinery & Why this refine plant matters

headline: Project Samridhi helps HPCL increase earnings by $0.54/bbl in FY26 - The HinduBusinessLine

The project is built around the philosophy of structural cost takeout and efficiency improvement, which involves the strategic reduction of fixed costs deeply embedded within operations, independent of business volumes, he added.

headline: Beyond the Balance Sheet: Westrock Coffee's Conway Bet Is Paying Off - BriefGlance.com
summary_text: Experts would likely conclude that Westrock Coffee's financial restructuring and operational milestones demonstrate a successful transition from heavy investment to sustainable profitability, validating its strategic bet on the Conway facility. ... On the surface, Westrock Coffee Company’s announcement today looks like standard corporate financial housekeeping. The beverage solutions provider extended the maturity on the bulk of its debt, shuffled its banking syndicate, and tweaked some loan covenants. These are moves that typically excite accountants and credit analysts but rarely capture broader attention. Yet, to dismiss this as mere balance sheet maintenance is to miss the real story: this is the financial echo of a massive operational victory, a signal that Westrock's audacious, multi-hundred-million-dollar bet on its Conway, Arkansas facility is beginning to pay off. ... In a strategic maneuver, the company extended the maturity date for approximately $361 million of its credit facilities to November 2028, providing a longer runway for its long-term plans. More tellingly, it terminated its covenant relief period well ahead of schedule. As CFO Chris Pledger noted, this provides “meaningful financial flexibility as we move beyond the peak investment phase of our Conway facility.” That single phrase, “peak investment phase,” is the key that unlocks the entire narrative. This isn't just about managing debt; it's about entering a new era of declining capital intensity and, crucially, improving free cash flow. ... To understand the significance of today’s financial news, one must first appreciate the sheer scale of the Conway project. Since 2021, Westrock has poured over $300 million into transforming a 524,000-square-foot facility into what is now the largest of its kind in the United States. This wasn't just an expansion; it was a fundamental reinvention of the company’s operational core, designed to shift its focus from traditional coffee roasting toward the higher-margin, high-growth world of ready-to-drink (RTD) beverages, extracts, and complex ingredients. ... The term “peak investment phase” is a stark understatement. Company filings show capital expenditures ballooning to approximately $160 million in 2024 as the facility was built out. That number fell to $89 million in 2025, and by the first quarter of 2026, it had plummeted to just $7 million. This dramatic drop is the clearest evidence that the heavy lifting is done. The massive capital sink that was Conway is now a fully commercialized, cash-flow-positive asset. With all five of its advanced production lines now operational, the facility that once consumed capital is now primed to generate it. ... This operational milestone is the direct enabler of the financial restructuring. The company’s lenders, a syndicate that now includes Texas Capital Bank, are not extending terms out of charity; they are responding to a fundamentally de-risked business profile. The proven performance of the Conway plant, which has effectively doubled Westrock's operational footprint, provides the confidence needed to offer more favorable terms. ... The details of the amended credit agreement read like a report card of a company that has earned its lenders' trust. By exiting the covenant relief period early, Westrock has voluntarily accepted a tighter leash. The maximum permitted secured net leverage ratio, a key measure of debt relative to earnings, will now be capped at 4.00x, down from a temporary ceiling of 5.00x. In corporate finance, offering to abide by stricter rules is a power move. It signals profound confidence from management that future earnings will comfortably support the debt load. ... for this confidence is immediate and tangible: lower borrowing costs. The early termination triggers a decrease in the applicable interest ... on its loans, which will directly reduce interest expenses and bolster the bottom line. According to one credit analyst, this move effectively trades temporary covenant flexibility for longer-term stability and lower costs—a trade any ... , growing company would make. ... This confidence is backed by tangible results. After a rocky period post-SPAC, Westrock's performance is showing a sharp upward trajectory. In the first quarter of 2026, the company more than tripled its consolidated adjusted EBITDA year-over-year to $26 million and swung from a $13.1 million operating loss to a $3.2 million operating income. Its secured net leverage ratio had already improved to 3.45x, well within the new, stricter covenant. The company isn’t just hoping for future performance; it’s already delivering it. ... This newfound financial flexibility isn't an end in itself; it's fuel for Westrock's strategic ambitions. The company is positioning itself as the essential behind-the-scenes partner for the world's largest brands, capitalizing on the biggest trends shaping the $5 trillion global beverage market. The “cold coffee revolution,” the explosive growth in functional beverages promising everything from energy to focus, and the unwavering consumer demand for convenience are all squarely in Conway’s wheelhouse. ... The plant's capabilities in canning, bottling, and producing complex extracts allow Westrock to move beyond being a private-label supplier and become an integrated solutions platform. It is already developing high-protein beverages for leading CPG brands and expanding its capabilities for milk-based RTD products and energy drinks. This aligns perfectly with a market where RTD beverages are projected to grow from $732 billion to over $1.2 trillion by 2032. ... Furthermore, this operational and financial stability reinforces the company's competitive advantage in sustainability. Westrock recently announced it had achieved 100% responsibly sourced green coffee and tea purchases, a powerful differentiator in a market of increasingly conscious consumers. Financial strength allows the company to maintain and expand these ethical sourcing programs, which are not just good for the world but are also good for business, attracting premium partners who value a transparent and traceable supply chain. ... For investors who have watched Westrock since its public debut, this moment feels like a turning point. The narrative is shifting from one of potential and investment to one of execution and monetization. The company has successfully navigated the most difficult and capital-intensive part of its transformation. The operational engine in Conway is running, the financial structure has been fortified, and the market trends are blowing squarely at its back. ... The road ahead will require continued discipline. Management has acknowledged the loss of a large single-serve customer due to M&A activity but projects it will backfill that capacity by 2027, driven by a strong sales pipeline for the new capabilities at Conway. Today’s announcement demonstrates that Westrock has secured the financial stability and runway necessary to see that strategy through. The focus now shifts from building the factory to filling it, proving that the massive bet on Conway can deliver the sustained profitability and growth the company has long promised.

headline: UPM-Sappi paper venture raises EU competition concerns
summary_text: - The European Commission warns that UPM and Sappi’s proposed joint venture could increase communication paper prices and reduce quality. - The companies argue that the €1.42 billion partnership would address declining demand, structural overcapacity, and high energy costs. - UPM and Sappi will formally respond to the EC’s preliminary concerns and continue discussions with regulators. ... The European Commission (EC) has informed UPM and Sappi that its proposed joint venture may restrict competition in the communication paper market. In May, UPM and Sappi signed a definitive agreement that proposed creating an independent, equal-owned partnership combining UPM’s global communication papers business and Sappi’s European graphic paper business. In a Statement of Objections, the EC explains that it is concerned that the proposed partnership could increase prices and decrease quality. It says that it is “currently unconvinced” that the joint venture would bring “enough benefits” in cost savings, environmental performance, or resilience improvements, to “offset the potential harm” of the merger. In April, the EC opened an investigation assessing whether the joint venture could reduce competition for certain communication papers in the European Economic Area (EEA), UK, and Switzerland. The investigation included analysis of internal documents provided by UPM and Sappi, and “views and data” from competitors, outlines the EC. ... UPM and Sappi estimate the enterprise value of the planned business combination to be €1.42 billion (US$1.65 billion). The UPM spokesperson outlines that the joint venture would contribute to the “resilience of the entire European graphic paper industry, in the interest of customers.” ... One of the EC’s responsibilities is to assess mergers and acquisitions involving companies with a turnover above certain thresholds. It aims to prevent concentrations that would “significantly impede” effective competition in the EEA. ... The Sappi spokesperson tells us that the rationale for the proposed joint venture “remains strong,” especially in a declining graphic paper market. The joint venture aims to rationalize supply in an industry facing declining demand, structural overcapacity, and high energy costs, according to the companies. ... A Statement of Objections is a formal procedure in any EC investigation into mergers and acquisitions. The EC states that the Statement of Objections “does not prejudge the outcome of the investigation,” but seeks to update the companies in writing of the formal objections against the joint venture. ... UPM and Sappi can now reply to the EC’s Statement of Objections, consult the case file, and request an oral hearing, as underscored by the EC. ... The companies will respond “in detail” to the EC’s concerns, says the UPM spokesperson, adding that these are confidential discussions on which it cannot comment further. ... “Sappi and UPM will submit their observations addressing the EC’s preliminary concerns and will continue to engage constructively with the EC to demonstrate the benefits of the transaction,” adds the Sappi spokesperson. ... Alongside amalgamated manufacturing processes, the packaging industry is entering a post-mega merger era, defined by consolidation, a prolonged downturn, and rising geopolitical uncertainty, say experts from Rabobank Packaging and Logistics. ... In a previous interview with Packaging Insights, Rabobank senior analysts Xinnan Li, Natasha Valeeva, and Jim Owen discussed shifting competitive dynamics, future growth prospects, and the increasing impact of regulation and private equity on the industry. ... In 2025, the EC approved International Paper’s acquisition of British e-commerce packaging giant DS Smith. Yet, a year after the merger, it announced plans to split into two regional, publicly traded companies. As part of the separation, its EMEA Packaging business will be spun off to shareholders, while IP intends to retain a meaningful ownership stake in the new company. ... In other recent business moves, Cosmogen acquired Asquan, an international premium personal care company headquartered in Hong Kong and Shenzhen, China, to consolidate its global reach in the personal care packaging space.

headline: EU challenges UPM and Sappi’s planned paper venture
summary_text: # UPM-Sappi deal could weaken competition, EU warns Sappi’s Kirkniemi paper mill near Lohja in Finland is due to become part of the planned joint venture with UPM. The European Commission fears the transaction could weaken competition in the printing paper market. Photo: Valmet. Published by Markku Björkman - 3 Sep, 2026 ... The European Commission has reached the preliminary conclusion that the proposed joint venture between Finland’s UPM and South Africa’s Sappi could restrict competition in the European printing paper market. Brussels fears that the transaction could enable the new company to raise prices or reduce product quality. ... The Commission has outlined its concerns in a statement of objections sent to the two forest industry groups. The document represents a formal step in the EU’s competition investigation and does not prejudge the final outcome of the case. ... According to Finnish public service broadcaster Yle, the planned joint venture would become the market leader in several categories of graphic paper across the European Economic Area, or EEA. ... The downturn has resulted in mill closures, production cuts and extensive restructuring across the European paper industry. ... The proposed company would combine UPM’s graphic paper operations in Europe and the United States with Sappi’s European business in the same sector. Selected parts of Sappi’s speciality paper activities and related operations would also be included. ... The European Commission’s concerns focus primarily on the markets for coated mechanical paper and coated woodfree paper. Its preliminary assessment indicates that the joint venture could obtain a sufficiently strong position to reduce competitive pressure. ... Greater market power could allow the company to raise prices or lower product quality to the detriment of customers. A highly concentrated market could also reduce customers’ choice of suppliers and weaken the incentive for producers to develop their products and services. ... The assessment is particularly significant because the transaction would combine two of Europe’s largest graphic paper producers. The Commission must now determine whether competition from other manufacturers and alternative products would be sufficient to constrain the new company. ... The investigation comes as European paper producers are already adjusting to a structurally contracting market. Companies argue that consolidation may be necessary to maintain efficient production, while customers remain concerned about the consequences of having fewer suppliers. ... UPM has said that it will review the Commission’s objections carefully together with Sappi and submit a formal response. ... The Finnish forest industry group remains confident that the companies can address the Commission’s preliminary concerns comprehensively. UPM has also stressed that the statement of objections forms part of the ongoing review and does not represent a final decision. ... According to UPM, the joint venture is a necessary step to safeguard long-term supplies of graphic paper to European customers. The company also argues that the transaction would help strengthen a European paper industry facing declining demand, high energy and raw-material costs, and excess production capacity. ... The companies’ case rests largely on the rapid transformation of the market. Structural demand for graphic paper has fallen for many years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain profitable production and sufficient capacity at European mills. ... The Commission must nevertheless assess whether the claimed industrial benefits outweigh the risk of customers having fewer suppliers from which to choose. ... UPM and Sappi signed the definitive agreement to establish the graphic paper joint venture in May 2026. ... UPM’s entire Communication Papers business would be transferred to the new company. Sappi would contribute its European graphic paper operations, selected speciality paper activities and associated functions. ... UPM and Sappi would each own 50 per cent of the joint venture. Neither company would therefore have sole control over the business. ... Sappi operates the Kirkniemi paper mill near Lohja in Finland. The facility is a major producer of coated paper used in magazines, advertising materials and other printed products. ... UPM, meanwhile, has extensive graphic paper production operations in Europe and the United States. The transaction would bring the companies’ mills, sales organisations and related activities together within one of the market’s largest producers. ... The parties now have an opportunity to respond to the Commission’s objections, provide additional evidence and propose measures to address the identified competition concerns. ... Possible remedies could include the sale of assets or other binding commitments. It is not yet known whether UPM and Sappi intend to offer concessions. ... The European Commission’s continued investigation will determine whether the joint venture can be approved in its current form, cleared subject to conditions or prohibited.

PM16 is not the first major grade shift at Riverdale. In 2017, International Paper announced an approximately $300 million conversion of PM15 from uncoated freesheet to high-quality whitetop linerboard and containerboard. At the time, the company said PM15 would add 450,000 tons of annual containerboard capacity and give the mill greater product flexibility. ... Now PM16 has followed with another $250 million investment. Together, the two projects represent roughly $550 million of announced conversion capital at the same Alabama mill in less than a decade. ... That is more revealing than treating PM16 as an isolated project. International Paper has repeatedly chosen to put major capital into Riverdale rather than abandon the site or replace it with a greenfield mill. The company is taking an existing industrial platform — fibre supply, energy, labour, maintenance, rail and truck logistics — and changing what that platform produces for the packaging market. ... Later in the Q2 call, Silvernail described International Paper’s North American strategy in unusually clear terms: the company wants to be the low-cost player, not the low-price player, and is integrating its mill and box networks more tightly so the right paper is made in the right locations and delivered with lower cost and better service. ... The immediate risk is not necessarily a sudden wave of extra containerboard. International Paper has not disclosed enough data to make that claim. ... The more important pressure could come from product mix and delivered economics. If Riverdale successfully qualifies more lightweight and high-performance grades, International Paper can combine paper production with its converting network and compete on the total economics of the package — paper performance, box design, logistics, reliability and service — rather than only on the price of a box. ... Before the conversion, Riverdale supplied Sylvamo with cutsize uncoated freesheet under an agreement linked to the companies’ 2021 separation. Sylvamo expected about 260,000 short tons from Riverdale in 2025 and around 100,000 short tons in 2026 before the agreement ended. ... As that supply disappeared, Sylvamo had to rebuild its North American sourcing plan using inventory, third-party conversion and imports from its own mills. Management said changes in U.S. tariff rates led it to bring more product from Brazil while reducing planned European imports. ... Its program includes a paper-machine optimization expected to add around 60,000 short tons of annual uncoated freesheet capacity and a new cutsize sheeter with 100,000 short tons of additional sheeting capability. ... But the chain reaction is important: one machine changes grade in Alabama, a former customer changes transatlantic sourcing, Brazilian and European flows move, another U.S. mill receives new capital, and International Paper redirects the original asset into containerboard. ... PM16 ramps on schedule, the intended grades qualify quickly and International Paper enters 2027 with a stronger Riverdale cost position and more lightweight and high-performance supply available to its packaging network. The pressure on competitors would come less from a dramatic capacity shock and more from improved cost, product mix and service from an integrated producer. ... Qualification and ramp-up proceed steadily, but the economics appear in stages. Full run rate is reached in Q1 2027 and the market gets a clearer view during 2027 of where the new grades are being used and which regional box markets benefit most. ... Qualification takes longer, operating stability is uneven or the final mix does not create the expected value. The $250 million project still operates, but the strategic and financial benefits take longer to show up. ... 1. Capacity disclosure — does International Paper finally provide an annual PM16 containerboard figure? 2. Grade mix — how much detail does the company give on lightweight and high-performance products? 3. Customer qualification — does management move from saying the machine is being qualified to describing meaningful commercial use across product lines? 4. Ramp timing — does Q1 2027 remain the full-run-rate target? 5. Network economics — do future results or management comments show measurable improvements in cost, reliability, freight or box-network performance linked to Riverdale? ... International Paper has spent $250 million and completed the mechanical conversion. Riverdale now has to prove that the new PM16 can make qualified containerboard at the cost, quality and consistency required by the packaging network. ... The larger strategic picture is already visible: about $550 million of announced investment across two Riverdale machine conversions, more than 750 people at a mill International Paper continues to back, and a corporate strategy built around making the right paper in the right place at a lower cost. ... For the corrugated board market, the key question is not simply how many tons PM16 can theoretically make. It is how many qualified, competitive tons International Paper can place into its box network — and what happens to regional customers, paper pricing and converter margins when it does. ... The conversion is complete. The biggest number is still missing. And the real market test begins now.

headline: ITC Completes Century Pulp and Paper Acquisition - Industrial Front
summary_text: ITC Limited has officially completed the integration of Century Pulp and Paper into its Paperboards and Specialty Papers Division (ITC-PSPD), pushing the company’s total paper and paperboard capacity up by more than 50% to approximately 1.5 million metric tonnes. The completion, announced on August 3, 2026, gives ITC its first major manufacturing footprint in northern India for this business and expands its access to key raw materials and customers in the region. ... Century Pulp and Paper was established in 1984 in Uttarakhand with an installed capacity of roughly 480,000 metric tonnes per annum, and ITC first agreed to acquire the unit from the Aditya Birla Group’s BK Birla side in April 2025. ITC Chairman and Managing Director Sanjiv Puri described the completed acquisition as a “defining milestone” for ITC-PSPD, which now becomes India’s largest integrated paperboards and paper business by capacity. ... ITC’s paperboards division has built its reputation on packaging board, specialty papers and value-added paperboard (VAP) products used across FMCG, pharmaceutical and cigarette packaging. Acquiring Century Pulp and Paper gives ITC-PSPD a strategically located production base in northern India, reducing its dependence on southern and eastern mills and cutting logistics costs for customers based in the north. The deal also expands ITC’s access to wood and pulp raw material sourcing in the Uttarakhand belt at a time when domestic wood prices have stayed elevated and import competition has squeezed margins across the paper sector. With capacity now near 1.5 million metric tonnes, ITC-PSPD strengthens its position against rivals such as JK Paper, West Coast Paper Mills and Emami Paper Mills, all of which have themselves expanded capacity over the past year. ... The completion of the Century Pulp deal comes as the Indian paper industry navigates a mix of pressures: elevated wood costs, competitively priced imports and a government-imposed Minimum Import Price (MIP) of Rs 67,220 per metric tonne on virgin multi-layer paperboard imports that runs until March 31, 2026. Larger, better-integrated players like ITC-PSPD are better placed to absorb these cost pressures than smaller regional mills, and the deal is likely to accelerate consolidation in India’s paperboard segment. It also signals confidence in long-term demand for sustainable, fibre-based packaging as brands shift away from single-use plastics under India’s tightened Extended Producer Responsibility rules. ... ITC shares have traded in a relatively tight band following the announcement, with the paperboards business representing one part of the diversified conglomerate’s broader FMCG, hotels and cigarettes portfolio. Within the paper trade press, the deal has been described as a strategic leap that gives ITC-PSPD a genuine pan-India manufacturing spread for the first time. Competing paper stocks, including JK Paper, Emami Paper Mills and West Coast Paper Mills, have separately rallied in recent sessions on strong quarterly results and import-price-linked pricing power, underscoring an industry-wide environment of consolidation and margin recovery even as individual companies pursue different growth strategies. ... ITC-PSPD is expected to spend the coming quarters integrating Century Pulp and Paper’s operations, including aligning production planning, sourcing and sales channels with its existing mills. Analysts will watch ITC’s upcoming quarterly results for early signs of synergy benefits and utilisation rates at the newly acquired Uttarakhand facility. The broader industry will also be watching whether the Minimum Import Price on paperboard imports is extended beyond its March 2026 deadline, a decision that will materially affect pricing power for ITC-PSPD and its rivals through the rest of the fiscal year. Investors and paper traders are also expected to track how quickly ITC-PSPD ramps up utilisation at the Uttarakhand facility and whether the company announces any further debottlenecking or brownfield expansion at its existing paperboard mills to complement the newly acquired capacity. ... Century Pulp and Paper was set up in 1984 in Uttarakhand with an installed capacity of about 480,000 metric tonnes per annum, giving ITC-PSPD a new manufacturing base in northern India. ... ITC’s total paper and paperboard capacity has grown by more than 50% following the Century Pulp and Paper integration, taking it to approximately 1.5 million metric tonnes. ... The deal makes ITC-PSPD India’s largest integrated paperboards and paper business by capacity, gives it a first major presence in northern India, and expands its access to raw materials and customers in that region.

headline: IP’s box volumes rise, but external conditions mute demand | Packaging Dive
summary_text: # IP’s box volumes rise, but external conditions mute demand International Paper expects geopolitical and economic conditions to offset some gains from recent price increases. Executives updated progress on the company’s split. Published July 30, 2026 Katie Pyzyk Lead Reporter International Paper’s broke ground on its greenfield box plant in Waterloo, Iowa, in May 2025. It expects startup in Q4 2026 and full production in early 2027. Courtesy of International Paper By the numbers: Q2 2026 Net sales: $6B Down 2.2% year over year EMEA packaging net sales: $2.29B Down 0.2% year over year Net loss: $12M Compared with a $75M net profit in Q2 2025 ... Even though International Paper had a particularly heavy outage schedule during the second quarter, roughly double typical levels, the company saw improvements in performance, said CEO Andy Silvernail during Thursday’s earnings call. ... He credited the ongoing work on the company’s optimization plan despite various economic and geopolitical challenges, such as the war with Iran and input cost inflation, mainly for OCC. ... Per-day box volumes in North America increased 1.7% year over year. Mill performance improved by approximatedly 500 basis points year over year. However, demand was “softer than we had expected” and inflation was significantly higher, Silvernail said, prompting the company to rework its expectations for demand growth in 2026. ... IP’s plan to split the company into two geographically-oriented businesses is reportedly on track to occur by early next year, as announced in January. Also, as suggested earlier this year, IP has accelerated ongoing cost removal actions in the Europe, Middle East and Africa region ahead of the split. To date, the company has achieved more than $210 million of run-rate savings in EMEA from closing 31 facilities and an office and from reducing headcount in the region by more than 3,000. ... Capital saved from the multitude of facility closures and employee separations during the last 18 months has been reinvested in areas with greater opportunities for returns, Silvernail said. He provided updates on four North American investments: two acquisitions and two facility build-outs. ... IP completed its acquisition of North Pacific Packaging Co. in June. The facility had impacts from the white liquor implosion disaster at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co.’s neighboring mill in Longview, Washington, in May, which left 11 people dead and eight others injured. ... While production at Norpac’s mill temporarily slowed during the NDP cleanup and investigation, Silvernail said, operations have returned to the pre-incident level. “Norpac is an excellent fit” for IP and allows for increased customer service on the West Coast. Also in Q2, IP completed the acquisition of Delmarva Corrugated Packaging in Delaware. This deal “strengthens our footprint in an attractive region” and supports long-term growth plans,” Silvernail said. ... The conversion of an uncoated freesheet machine at the Riverdale mill in Selma, Alabama, to produce containerboard is complete, and ramp-up is going according to schedule. ... IP still expects to start up a new greenfield box plant in Waterloo, Iowa, during the fourth quarter with full production slated for Q2 2027. ... Investments to enhance IP’s presence in certain geographic locations boost responsiveness to customers, which plays into the company’s optimization plan. “Responsiveness goes up, cost comes down,” Silvernail said. ... Just days before the earnings call, IP announced its third containerboard price increase of 2026, for $80 per ton, to take effect Sept. 1; that follow’s Packaging Corporation of America’s announcement of a $140 per ton increase, widely called unprecedented. IP executives expect that increase to be fully realized by Q1 to Q2 2027. ... “Obviously we would expect some of it to flow through attractively to the bottom line, but we'll have to see kind of what happens” in the coming months, given challenging external conditions like the war, Silvernail said. Energy and OCC price inflation is expected to offset some of the gains. ... IP anticipates a “step-up” in its North American earnings for the second half of the year. The region’s full-year adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization is $2.35 billion to $2.45 billion, lowering the top range by about $50 million, executives said. “There’s a lot of uncertainty out there with what’s happening in the Middle East,” Silvernail said, in addition to other factors including inflation, so IP now does not expect demand to increase notably in the second half of 2026. It now expects relatively flat demand in North America and a modest uptick in Europe. “And we’ll see what that means for ‘27,” he said.

A non-binding letter of intent (LOI) on the transaction was signed on December 4, 2025. headline: Arbex debuts with R$18bn in revenue as Suzano expands tissue business
summary_text: Arbex debuts with R$18bn in revenue as Suzano expands tissue business ... # Arbex debuts with R$18bn in revenue as Suzano expands tissue business ... ## Suzano, Kimberly-Clark’s new tissue JV, targets $175m in efficiency gains over three years ... es — São Paulo 02/07/2026 07h37 Atualizado 02/07/2026 07h37 Beto Abreu, CEO of Suzano — Foto: Rogerio Vieira/Valor Created by Suzano and U.S.-based Kimberly-Clark, Arbex debuts as one of the world's largest tissue paper companies. The joint venture, completed on Wednesday (1) and valued at $3.7 billion (R$19.2 billion at current exchange rates), launches with annual revenue of $3.5 billion (R$18.1 billion) and aims to become the most efficient integrated tissue company in the global industry. Suzano, which announced a year ago the acquisition of a 51% stake in Kimberly-Clark’s global tissue operations outside the U.S., holds a controlling stake in the new company. Kimberly-Clark owns the remaining 49%. “Our ambition is not to be the largest company in the sector, but the most efficient,” Suzano CEO Beto Abreu told Valor. ... Arbex’s initial business plan is centered on that goal, prioritizing cost reductions to improve efficiency over the short and medium term. “We have publicly committed to generating $175 million in operational efficiencies over the next three years. Before thinking about the next stage of growth, we need to deliver on that commitment. We need to earn the right to grow, and that is our objective in the short and medium term,” he said. At the same time, the transaction strengthens Suzano’s strategy to expand pulp sales. As part of its strategy to replace softwood pulp with hardwood pulp, Suzano plans to accelerate Arbex’s adoption of hardwood fiber, where the Brazilian company holds a competitive edge. “We will accelerate that process within Arbex,” Abreu said. ... Suzano had already been the exclusive supplier of hardwood pulp to all Kimberly-Clark operations. Under the new structure, it will remain the exclusive supplier indefinitely for the businesses now housed within Arbex. “When manufacturing products such as paper towels and toilet paper, you can use anywhere from 70% to 100% hardwood pulp, with the remainder being softwood. That transition will now accelerate because we operate the machines that previously belonged to Kimberly-Clark’s international business,” Abreu explained. ... Arbex now encompasses Kimberly-Clark’s production and sales of products such as toilet paper, napkins, paper towels, and facial tissues outside the United States. The transaction also transfers 22 manufacturing facilities across 14 countries in Europe, Asia, the Middle East, South America, Central America, Africa, and Oceania to the new company. ... Headquartered in the Netherlands with an operational office in London, Arbex owns a portfolio of over 40 regional brands and holds long-term licenses for Kimberly-Clark’s global brands, including Kleenex, Cottonelle, Scott, WypAll, Viva, and Kimberly-Clark Professional. ... Suzano formally assumed control of the new company on Wednesday (1) after paying $1.3 billion for its 51% stake. By announcing the transaction, the partners disclosed that Suzano would have the option to acquire the remaining 49% at any time, using the same valuation multiple—6.5 times earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA)—that determined the original purchase price. According to Abreu, however, Suzano has no intention of exercising that option in the short or medium term. “We like the partnership because our capabilities are complementary. We bring industrial operating expertise, while they contribute brand strength and product development,” he said. Abreu said the efficiency gains outlined in Arbex’s business plan will come primarily from lower manufacturing and administrative costs, the development of regional suppliers, and supply chain optimization. “We have many tools and technologies that can generate significant gains in logistics throughout the supply chain and distribution process from Arbex’s plants to customers in 70 countries,” he said. For Suzano, Kimberly-Clark’s decision to divest part of its international operations reflects its confidence that the Brazilian company can unlock greater value from those assets. “I imagine they believe the company will generate more value under our management than it would under theirs alone, because a global multinational does not always have the same speed to advance certain strategic initiatives,” Abreu said. The new company’s leadership combines executives from both partners. Ehab Abou-Oaf, who already headed the international operations now integrated into Arbex, remains CEO. Luís Bueno, formerly Suzano’s executive vice president for consumer goods, becomes chief operating officer, while Oscar Mousinho, formerly chief financial officer of Mars’s animal nutrition business, assumes the CFO role. “We have the prerogative to appoint the CEO and CFO, but we chose to recommend the current CEO because of his experience and brought in a CFO from outside the company,” Abreu said. According to Abreu, Arbex will operate independently from both Suzano and Kimberly-Clark. Its financial results, however, will be fully consolidated into Suzano’s financial statements and reported separately from the tissue business Suzano already operates in Brazil. The new company’s board of directors will be chaired by Walter Schalka, Suzano’s former CEO. Other board members include Carlos Aníbal Fernandes de Almeida Júnior, Suzano’s executive vice president for Europe; Fabricio Bloisi Rocha, CEO of Prosus, the parent company of iFood; Kimberly-Clark CFO Nelson Urdaneta; and Kimberly-Clark Chief Strategy Officer Jeffrey Meluci. Asked about the possibility of further acquisitions, Abreu said the company’s current priority is “deleveraging and generating value from investments already made before considering new moves.” He added that the $1.3 billion cash payment is not expected to increase Suzano’s leverage materially. Citi analysts said the creation of Arbex marks a milestone for Suzano given the size of the investment. They said investors are now likely to focus on the company’s ability to rebuild cash generation and expect Arbex’s operating volumes to begin being consolidated into Suzano’s results starting in the third quarter. On the day Arbex was launched, Suzano’s shares rose 2.1%, the second-best performance on the Ibovespa, closing at R$40.59. The stock, however, remains down 21.1% so far this year, according to Valor Data. The purpose of the PPWR is to reduce packaging waste and its environmental impact. The regulation covers the entire lifecycle of packaging – from product design to waste management. "PPWR sets the direction, but it is up to the industry to develop the solutions needed to reach the goals. At the same time, harmonized rules within the EU create more equal competitive conditions and make it easier to develop solutions for the European common market.
